Leadership development does not happen in a single program—it happens through a series of experiences.

This Resource Bank is curated by DKU Leadership Programs to help students discover high-quality opportunities inside and outside Duke Kunshan University, including Fellowships, Event, Conference, and other developmental experiences.

You can browse resources by the following categories:

On-Campus Opportunities: Opportunities offered within the DKU community that allow students to engage in leadership, research, employment, governance, or campus life while enrolled. These opportunities are typically organized by DKU offices, academic divisions, or student organizations and often involve ongoing responsibilities or recurring engagement throughout a semester or academic year.

Fellowship: Highly selective programs that support students or recent graduates through funding, mentorship, leadership development, research, service, or professional experiences. Fellowships usually require a competitive application process and extend over a defined period, ranging from several weeks to multiple years.

Experiential Programs: Hands-on learning opportunities that enable students to apply knowledge and skills in real-world contexts. These experiences emphasize learning through practice, reflection, and active engagement with communities, organizations, industries, or research environments, rather than through formal instruction alone.

Events & Conferences: Short-term events designed for learning, networking, dialogue, or idea exchange. These opportunities are typically completed in a single day or over several consecutive days and may include conferences, forums, summits, workshops, symposiums, hackathons, or competitions.

Training Programs: Structured learning programs consisting of multiple sessions delivered over a period of time. Training programs are designed to systematically develop specific knowledge, competencies, or leadership skills through a sequenced curriculum, often combining workshops, coaching, assignments, and reflection activities.

The Duke Kunshan Student Leaders Board (SLB) is a body of student leaders, endorsed by peers and appointed by the University, to represent and serve student interests and needs in collaboration and consultation with the University leadership. Members of the SLB identify students’ needs and concerns, provide insights for campus decision-makers, create or co-create initiatives and programs, and engage in constructive and collaborative dialogue to promote the overall welfare and experience of student peers and the DKU community.

2.value: Students who guide new students through pre-arrival, Orientation Week, and the first 7 weeks of DKU102

Resident Assistants (RAs) are upperclass undergraduate or graduate students whose role is to help residents feel at home while living in our residence halls by creating opportunities to live, learn, and lead. To assist in residents’ academic and social integration at DKU, RAs host events that extend learning beyond the classroom, enhance a sense of belonging in their area, and encourage self-discovery. RAs serve as role model student leaders who take time to get to know and promote individual residents’ growth and development. They represent the depth and breadth of diversity in our student body. Additionally, RAs serve in a critical after-hours “on duty” capacity, responding to various inconveniences, emergencies, and crises.

4.value: RAs: Candidates must be upperclass undergraduate or graduate students at DKU.

2.value: A highly selective, fully funded one-year fellowship for exceptional student leaders from around the world to study at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. The program combines rigorous academics (30-36 credit hours per year), leadership development workshops, and cultural immersion. Fellows receive full funding for tuition, fees, living expenses, and enrichment opportunities. Upon completion, students receive an official UNC transcript and a certificate from the Morehead-Cain Foundation, and they return to their home institution to graduate

4.value: Current undergraduates; completed at least two years of study; expected to graduate after January 2028
